title: Incident Response

header.html: 5.3 Understand Incident Response (IR): Data handling policy implementing Incident Response Plan (IRP); Incident Response (IR) exercises (for example testing, tabletop)
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

html:
1Events, incidents and the plan

Term Meaning
Event Any observable occurrence in a system
Incident An event that actually or potentially harms confidentiality, integrity or availability, or breaks policy
Breach An incident in which protected data is disclosed to unauthorized people

An incident response plan (IRP) is the documented plan for how the organization detects, handles and learns from incidents. It lists roles, severity levels, steps, contacts and communication rules. An incident response team has members from security, IT, legal, communications, HR and management.

Exam tip

. The plan is written before the incident. During an incident follow the plan; do not improvise.

2The incident response phases

Phase What happens
1 Preparation Plan, team, tools, training, contacts, tested playbooks
2 Detection and analysis Spot the incident (alerts, reports), confirm it, rate its severity, scope it
3 Containment Limit the damage: isolate hosts, disable accounts, block addresses
4 Eradication Remove the cause: delete malware, close the vulnerability, patch
5 Recovery Restore systems from clean backups, monitor for return
6 Post-incident activity Lessons learned: review what happened, update the plan and controls

Phases 3 to 5 are grouped as containment, eradication and recovery in the NIST guide. Containment comes before eradication: stop the spread first, then clean.

Exam tip

. Prepare, detect and analyze, contain, eradicate, recover, learn. Contain first: do not delete evidence or rebuild before you understand and limit the attack.

3Data handling in the plan

A data handling policy tells responders how to treat information during an incident.

Rule Fact
Classification applies Incident data (logs, copies of systems) is handled by its sensitivity
Need to know Share details only with those who must know
Legal and regulatory notice Laws may require telling regulators or customers within a deadline; legal counsel decides
Communication One spokesperson; do not discuss on public channels

Evidence handling:

Concept Meaning
Chain of custody A record of who held the evidence and when, so it stays trustworthy
Order of volatility Collect the most short-lived data first: memory, then running processes and network state, then disk, then logs and backups
Forensic copy and hash Work on a copy; a hash proves the copy matches the original
Exam tip

. Chain of custody keeps evidence admissible. Memory is collected before disk because it disappears when the power is off.

4Exercises and testing

A plan that is never tested fails when needed.

Exercise What happens Impact
Read-through / checklist Team reviews the plan None
Tabletop Team discusses a scenario around a table None on systems
Walkthrough Team steps through actual procedures Low
Simulation Acts out a scenario, possibly with test systems Low
Full exercise Real actions against live or realistic systems Higher

After each exercise, record findings and update the plan.

Automation and AI: playbooks and automated tools handle routine, repeatable steps such as blocking a known bad address; a person decides about serious or unusual incidents.

5Related plans

Plan Relationship
IRP Handles the security incident
Disaster recovery plan Restores IT if the incident destroys systems
Business continuity plan Keeps the business running while it is handled

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A malware infection is confirmed on a server. What should the team do first?

  • AContain the incident by isolating the server
  • BReinstall the server to remove all traces of it
  • CWrite the final report of the incident
  • DDelete the logs to save disk space
Show the answer

Answer: A. Containment limits the damage and comes before eradication and recovery.

S2Which phase includes removing malware and closing the vulnerability that allowed the attack?

  • ADetection and analysis
  • BEradication
  • CContainment
  • DPreparation
Show the answer

Answer: B. Eradication removes the cause of the incident.

S3After an incident, the team meets to review what happened and improve the plan. Which phase is this?

  • APost-incident activity, which captures lessons learned
  • BRecovery, which restores the systems
  • CPreparation, which builds the team
  • DContainment, which isolates the systems
Show the answer

Answer: A. The review and plan update belong to post-incident activity.

S4Which data should a responder collect first from a running compromised computer?

  • AThe hard drive, which is stored permanently on the device
  • BMemory contents, which are lost at power off
  • CArchived backups, which are kept offline
  • DOld logs, which are kept on the server
Show the answer

Answer: B. The order of volatility says to collect memory first because it disappears when power is lost.

S5A team talks through a ransomware scenario around a table without touching any system. What is this exercise?

  • AA full exercise with real actions
  • BA penetration test of the network
  • CA disaster recovery failover test
  • DA tabletop exercise that is a discussion
Show the answer

Answer: D. A discussion-based scenario exercise is a tabletop exercise.

S6A record shows who held a disk image, when and where it was stored. What does this record support?

  • AChain of custody of the evidence
  • BNon-repudiation of the sender
  • CLeast privilege of the analyst
  • DSeparation of duties in the team
Show the answer

Answer: A. A record of who held evidence and when is the chain of custody.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What are the phases of incident response?

Show the answer

Preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, post-incident activity.

R2What does an IRP list?

Show the answer

Roles, severity levels, steps, contacts and communication rules.

R3What is chain of custody?

Show the answer

A record of who held the evidence and when.

R4Which data is collected first by the order of volatility?

Show the answer

Memory.

R5Does a tabletop exercise touch real systems?

Show the answer

No, it is a discussion.

R6Who decides about legal notification of a breach?

Show the answer

Legal counsel with management.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Definitions event, incident (harm or threat), breach (data disclosed)
Phases prepare, detect and analyze, contain, eradicate, recover, learn
Data handling classification, need to know, legal notice, one spokesperson
Evidence chain of custody, order of volatility, hashed copy
Exercises read-through, tabletop, walkthrough, simulation, full
